newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria shares end 0.69 pct higher at 3-year high.
newsitem.headline: Austria shares end 0.69 pct higher at 3-year high.

text.p: Austrian shares ploughed higher on Wednesday to end at a new three-year high, holding above the important psychological 1,200-point mark, and most traders saw potential for further gains.
The 21 blue chip ATX index climbed 8.26 points or 0.69 percent to 1,208.49. Among its constituents 15 stocks rose, five fell and one was unchanged.
"Cash is flowing into the big shares, why shouldn't we be able to reach 1,240 points?" one trader said.

Another predicted the index could rise to 1,220, but noted the air was already thin at the current level. He saw a slight correction of around 10 points in the near future due to falling turnover, in spite of the rise in prices.
Traders said interest centred on market heavyweights.
"There was demand for some of the blue chips, but I think that's been exhausted," one said.
Technical analysts said the index's increase looked promising but also doubted the breakthrough would be sustainable due to the meagre turnover.
Austrian microchip maker AMS was the top gainer, adding 4.86 percent at 1,143 schillings.
Preferred shares of Bank Austria led the decliners, dropping 1.16 percent to 425 schillings.
The ATX February future gained 6.0 points to 1,209.0.
The broad-based Vienna bourse index ended 2.0 points or 0.45 percent higher at 448.96.
